tool.title: Collect candidate translations from open engines
tool.description: Ask one or more open, self-hosted machine translators — OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP Marian models, CC-BY 4.0, run locally) and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate (AGPL, Argos models) — for CANDIDATE translations of each empty or fuzzy string, so no freemium API quota is involved. Candidates are appended to `<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`) for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page; a candidate whose placeholders or markup do not round-trip is not recorded. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an EMPTY msgstr gets the first good candidate, marked `#, fuzzy`; a non-empty msgstr is never overwritten. The translation node records the source (`generatedBy: "machine"`, model, time); `official` is never set, and a candidate is never a verdict. A catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or whose node is official, gets candidates but no fill.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The layer root whose declared `translation-sources` directory is filled. Default: the current directory.

inputs.name: engines
inputs.description: Comma-separated candidate sources, tried in this order for an empty msgstr: `opus-mt` (the local runner `scripts/translation/opus_mt_runner.py`, shared with `translate-pot`, which needs the extended Python tier) and/or `libretranslate` (the URL below). Absent, the command exits 2.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: A self-hosted LibreTranslate's base URL (default `http://localhost:5000`). The hosted libretranslate.com / .de services are refused.

inputs.name: locales
inputs.description: Comma-separated locales to fill, e.g. `es,fr`. Default: every locale directory except the source locale.

inputs.name: init
inputs.description: Start a `.po` from each template that has none (locale named, `X-Folio-Official: no`, every msgstr empty), then collect candidates for it. Never the default: starting a catalogue is a decision.

inputs.name: noCreateNode
inputs.description: Record candidates for a catalogue with no translation node beside it, but fill nothing there, instead of writing a minimal `translation-node/v1` for it.

inputs.name: noMask
inputs.description: Send placeholders to the engine as they are, instead of as numbered stand-ins. The round-trip check runs either way.

outputs.name: candidates
outputs.description: `translations/<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`), appended to: each candidate carries its text and source `{kind: "open-mt", id: <model>, version?, at}`. Identical text from the same source is not added twice.

outputs.name: catalogues
outputs.description: The `.po` catalogues whose empty msgstr got the first good candidate, `#, fuzzy`, and their `<name>.json` translation nodes. Exit 0 something was recorded · 3 nothing was · 2 could not determine · 1 an engine failed.

selection.when: A catalogue has empty or fuzzy entries and machine drafts are wanted for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page. Every candidate is a draft; a person's adjudication decides.
selection.limits: Singular entries only: plural entries are left for a person. Catalogues that say DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, and catalogues whose node is official, are refused. Machine output into a language nobody on the project reads cannot be checked here; it is a draft for review, never a sign-off. The LibreTranslate host is whatever `--url` names (normally one on this machine), so it has no fixed remedy; without one, use `--engine opus-mt`.
selection.cost: OPUS-MT: a model download per language pair on first use (hundreds of MB) and CPU time, no per-string fee. LibreTranslate: whatever running your own instance costs.

remedies.none: OPUS-MT downloads each model once; with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and a model already in the cache, or `--runner` pointing at a runner with `--model-dir`, it runs with no network.

$comment.comment: The owner, 2026-11-14: an unrestricted, open machine-translation step for the gettext catalogues, so no freemium API quota is involved; then, the same day, several translation sources per string as CANDIDATES a reviewer chooses among, and candidates are never a barrier to having a translation. It replaces the DeepL / Google Translate `po-translate` route `translation-manager` §3 used to recommend. Paid services (DeepL, Google Cloud Translation, Azure Translator, Amazon Translate) are deliberately not engines here (owner: mention, do not add). The engines are adapters in the implementing layer's `scripts/lib/translation-sources/`; the one writer is `scripts/lib/translation-candidates.ts` `addCandidates`, which a translation-platform import (Weblate, Crowdin, Transifex, `kind: "web-service"`) calls too.

`translation-refresh` §4 is where a first draft of the new and fuzzy strings is made, and the step that names this Tool. A machine string stays fuzzy, so §4's own rule (clear `#, fuzzy` only on an entry actually re-translated) still holds: this Tool never clears one. `translation-candidate-source` (cat-harness#1331) is the interface every candidate engine meets: what it writes, the translation-candidates/v1 sidecar and the fuzzy seed of an empty msgstr. This Tool writes exactly that, through the shared writer.
